Wendy's has significantly better salads. And even Wendy's cheap burgers come with lettuce and tomato. I am surprised that McDonald's has failed to keep up. But I expect if they were still raking in the money, then there was no huge incentive to dramatically improve their menu.

I don't have a problem with people who buy organic foods. I have a major problem with the difference between what you'll find in organic foods and what you'll expect to find. When people hear "organic" they think it means "no pesticides". What it actually means is "nothing from this list of "unnatural" pesticides but you can use all the 'natural' ones you like." This leads to toxic levels of pesticides being eaten without proper washing and preparation.

And some of the definitions are strict in all the wrong ways. A farmer can't raise legacy apples without pesticides, juice them, and sell the juice as organic. That's because the fiber content from plain apple juice doesn't fit the official definition. He can call his apple juice "all natural", but then so can a farmer who owns 2,000 acres, coats them in evil shit, and hires illegal immigrants with syphilis to pick them for $2 per hour and a cot.

We need new definitions and a strict, no-bullshit certification agency for organics. Anything else is literally toxic.
